stem.text: The diagram shows how the $\beta$-glucose units of cellulose are linked to each other.

stem.alt: Displayed structural formula of linked glucose units forming a cellulose chain, with CH2OH and OH groups labelled and an O bridge between units.

stem.text: What is the significance of the fact that the $\text{OH}$ groups on carbon 2 in adjacent glucose molecules are on opposite sides of the molecule?

A.text: They can cross-link with other cellulose molecules by both hydrogen and glycosidic bonds.

B.text: They can form glycosidic bonds with adjacent $\text{OH}$ groups of other cellulose molecules.

C.text: They can form hydrogen bonds between the $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ and $\text{OH}$ on adjacent glucose molecules of the cellulose molecule.

D.text: They can form hydrogen bonds with adjacent $\text{OH}$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ groups of other cellulose molecules.
